title: Analytic expressions for topological index data
notes: Nirenberg's report is analytic without explicit topology. The scan says the connection to topology and the disappearance of lower-order terms are unclear; the supplied transcription instead says “no connections” and “leading terms”. Gelfand replies that Atiyah--Singer and Pontryagin classes also have analytic expressions.
statement: The Fredholm index of an elliptic operator on a closed manifold depends on the topological class of its principal symbol. Characteristic classes have differential-form representatives constructed from connections, allowing analytic integral formulae for topological invariants.
reconstruction: The corrected readings are \ru{неясна связь} and \ru{младшие члены}. No particular degree map or characteristic polynomial is supplied. Independence of the index under lower-order perturbations must be distinguished from dependence of a chosen local density representative.
fate: The index theorem predates this seminar; the analytic construction actually developed next is Seeley's \citep[pp.~96--98]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established background; no separate conjecture is specified.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Positive spectra of the two Laplacians
notes: For \(\lambda>0\), \(E_\lambda(L^*L)\) and \(E_\lambda(LL^*)\) have common dimension \(d_\lambda\); the identification explicitly excludes zero.
statement: Let \(L:C^\infty(M;E)\to C^\infty(M;F)\) be elliptic of positive order on a closed smooth manifold with Hermitian bundles and a smooth positive density. For \(\lambda>0\), \(L:E_\lambda(L^*L)\to E_\lambda(LL^*)\) is an isomorphism with inverse \(\lambda^{-1}L^*\). Moreover \(\ker L^*L=\ker L\) and \(\ker LL^*=\ker L^*\).
reconstruction: The inverse and analytic setting are supplied. Direct composition proves the eigenspace assertion; \(\langle L^*Lu,u\rangle=\|Lu\|^2\) proves the kernel assertion.
fate: This elementary spectral argument is the input to the complex-power index calculation \citep[p.~96]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard and correct under the stated domain hypotheses.

title: Spectral complex powers and traces
notes: For \(\operatorname{Re}s\ll0\), \((I+L^*L)^s\) has an eigenfunction kernel whose integrated diagonal gives \(\sum d_\lambda(1+\lambda)^s\).
statement: If \(L\) has order \(r>0\), \(A=I+L^*L\) has order \(2r\). For \(\operatorname{Re}s<-n/(2r)\), \(A^s\) is trace class and \(\operatorname{Tr}A^s=\sum_j(1+\lambda_j)^s\), counting multiplicity. The kernel is distributionally \(\sum_j(1+\lambda_j)^s\Psi_j(x)\Psi_j(y)^*\); sufficiently negative real part gives continuity and the diagonal trace integral.
reconstruction: One may sum over distinct eigenvalues with multiplicities, or over a full eigenbasis without an additional multiplicity factor. The convergence threshold and bundle adjoint are supplied.
fate: Spectral calculus is the known starting point for the continuation in \citet[pp.~96--97]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard with convergence qualifications.

title: Regularized trace difference and index
notes: All positive-eigenvalue terms cancel in \(\operatorname{Tr}(I+L^*L)^s-\operatorname{Tr}(I+LL^*)^s\), leaving \(\dim\ker L-\dim\ker L^*\), independent of \(s\).
statement: Initially for \(\operatorname{Re}s<-n/(2r)\), the difference of the two traces equals \(\operatorname{ind}L\). Their meromorphic continuations therefore have the same constant difference, in particular at a common regular point such as zero.
reconstruction: At zero the separately unregularized traces are not finite. The continuation identity follows from the identity theorem applied to the trace-class half-plane.
fate: The cancellation is elementary and underlies the local formula \citep[pp.~96--98]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; regularization must remain explicit.

title: Contour powers with a spectral cut
notes: An angular gap about the negative ray is assumed for the principal symbol; powers use a resolvent contour and multiplication by integer powers. A parenthesis proposes reducing to order one by multiplication by an invertible operator.
statement: Let \(A\) be an invertible classical elliptic operator of positive order \(m\) on a closed manifold, with a ray avoided by its principal-symbol spectra and operator spectrum. Fix a branch and oriented contour. Then \(A^s=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_\Gamma\lambda^s(\lambda-A)^{-1}d\lambda\), initially for negative real part, extends by integer powers to a holomorphic family satisfying \(A^sA^t=A^{s+t}\). The parameter resolvent estimate applies along the contour.
reconstruction: The symbol condition concerns eigenvalues in the bundle case; invertibility and an operator spectral cut are added. Order reduction can simplify an index problem but does not preserve individual powers or kernels under arbitrary multiplication.
fate: Seeley's circulated preprint contains this construction; its Russian translation appeared in 1968 \citep[pp.~96--97]{seeley1968powers}. Nirenberg is reporting another author's work.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard spectral-cut calculus.

title: Holomorphic kernels in a left half-plane
notes: Assertion (i) says \(s\mapsto K_s\) is holomorphic into \(C^k\) when \(\operatorname{Re}(ms)<-n-k\).
statement: Under the spectral-cut hypotheses of the preceding item, the distribution kernel of \(A^s\) is a holomorphic family; for \(\operatorname{Re}(ms)<-n-k\) its values are in \(C^k(M\times M)\), holomorphically in that topology.
reconstruction: The operator acts on a smooth bundle over a closed \(n\)-manifold. The stated threshold ensures enough negative order for the kernel derivatives to be continuous.
fate: This is the first kernel assertion of \citet[p.~97]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established for classical elliptic operators with a spectral cut.

title: Entire continuation off the diagonal
notes: Assertion (ii) takes a compact set in \(M\times M\) disjoint from the diagonal and continues the restricted kernels holomorphically over the whole \(s\)-plane.
statement: For every compact subset \(C\subset M\times M\setminus\operatorname{diag}M\), the kernel of \(A^s\) depends entirely on \(s\) as a smooth function on a neighbourhood of \(C\), with every \(C^\infty\) seminorm controlled locally in \(s\).
reconstruction: Smoothness in \(x,y\) is not real analyticity; the notebook itself warns that the coefficients are only infinitely differentiable.
fate: This is the off-diagonal kernel assertion of \citet[p.~97]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the classical elliptic calculus.

title: Meromorphic continuation of the diagonal density
notes: Assertion (iii) gives possible simple poles at \((j-n)/m\), omitting zero because it is regular.
statement: The initially defined diagonal \(K_s(x,x)\) has meromorphic continuation, with at most simple poles among \((j-n)/m\), \(j\in\mathbb N_0\). The candidate pole at zero is removable; other possible poles may cancel. This is a continued density-valued endomorphism.
reconstruction: Continuation is performed after taking the diagonal in a half-plane where it is defined. It is not a general distributional restriction operation.
fate: The candidate poles and regularity at zero are in \citet[p.~97]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the distinction from the full zero-power kernel is treated next.

title: Exponent zero versus diagonal continuation
notes: The manuscript says \ru{при \(s=0\) это не единичный оператор}, with the explanation that the kernel is not a delta function.
statement: As an operator \(A^0=I\), whose full distribution kernel is the identity delta distribution. The finite value at zero of the meromorphically continued diagonal \(K_s(x,x)\) results from restricting first in a left half-plane and then continuing. It is not the diagonal restriction of the full kernel of \(A^0\).
reconstruction: This corrects a conflation in the handwritten source, not a mistranscription. Acting on each eigenvector verifies \(A^0=I\) directly.
fate: The functional calculus and continued diagonal in \citet[pp.~96--97]{seeley1968powers} distinguish these operations.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal operator assertion is false; the intended regularized-diagonal distinction is valid.

title: Local resolvent coefficient and index density
notes: The notes write \((2\pi)^nK_0(x,x)=m^{-1}\int_{|\xi|=1}\int_{-\infty}^0b_{-m-n}(x,\xi;\lambda)\,d\lambda\,dS\), then take the difference of such expressions for the index.
statement: Continue the diagonal densities of \((I+L^*L)^s\) and \((I+LL^*)^s\) to zero. The integral of the difference of their fibre traces is \(\operatorname{ind}L\). Each local continued density is computable from the parameter-resolvent symbol term of degree \(-m-n\), with its resolvent-sign and contour conventions fixed consistently.
reconstruction: The coefficient formula is recorded in Seeley's convention. Replacing \((A-\lambda)^{-1}\) by \((\lambda-A)^{-1}\) changes the coefficient sign; the contour must change consistently. The invariant assertion is the integrated difference.
fate: The coefficient expression is \citet[p.~97, formula (II)]{seeley1968powers}; it is the close publication match.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established analytic index machinery.

title: Complex powers remain pseudodifferential
notes: The final paragraph says \(A^s\) is pseudodifferential, with a symbol obtained by inserting the symbol in the contour formula.
statement: For an invertible classical elliptic operator of order \(m>0\) with a spectral cut, \(A^s\) is classical of complex order \(ms\). Its homogeneous symbol coefficients are obtained by contour integration of the parameter-resolvent symbol expansion.
reconstruction: The substitution is in the full symbolic calculus: lower-order derivative corrections are present. It is generally false that the exact symbol is just the pointwise scalar power \(a(x,\xi)^s\).
fate: This is the symbol construction of \citet[pp.~97--99]{seeley1968powers}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; its symbol calculation supplies the preceding local density formula.

title: Unlabelled finite configurations
notes: Collision-free labelled configurations map to \(N\)-point subsets \(C_{\Omega,N}\). Symmetry of \(H\) allows the Hamiltonian and Gibbs measure to descend; the discarded collision set has measure zero.
statement: For bounded Borel \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^\nu\), quotient the collision-free subset of \(\Omega^N\) by permutations. A symmetric measurable Hamiltonian with positive finite partition function defines a Gibbs probability, whose pushforward is a law on simple \(N\)-point configurations. Lebesgue reference measure gives all collision diagonals measure zero.
reconstruction: The \(1/N!\) factor belongs consistently to the quotient reference measure or to both normalized integrals. The null-set claim presupposes a non-atomic reference measure.
fate: The construction is explicit in \citet[\S1, pp.~60--62]{minlos1967limiting} and \citet[Lecture II]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard configuration-space probability.

title: Counting-cylinder sigma algebra
notes: \(C_\infty\) consists of finite or countable subsets without accumulation points; the sigma algebra is generated by \(n(d,U_i)=k_i\) for finite collections of disjoint sets.
statement: Let \(\Gamma\) be the locally finite simple configurations in \(\mathbb R^\nu\), with the sigma algebra generated by \(N_U(\gamma)=|\gamma\cap U|\) for bounded Borel \(U\). Finite intersections of counting events generate it; disjoint observation sets suffice by a finite Boolean refinement.
reconstruction: Bounded Borel sets and ambient local finiteness specify the intended measurable space.
fate: This is the space used in Minlos's forthcoming construction \citep[\S1]{minlos1967limiting}; A marks the exact authorial publication, not a claim of novelty for counting cylinders.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the standard measurable configuration space.

title: Dilute limiting Gibbs distribution
notes: The notes ask for a limiting space with the finite-volume asymptotic properties and say existence is proved at low density.
statement: A verified precise version is grand canonical: for stable pair interactions with integrable Mayer function, and sufficiently small activity at fixed \(\beta>0\), the low-activity expansion constructs a translation-invariant probability law on locally finite configurations with the limiting local distributions. A concrete subclass consists of hard-core finite-range potentials bounded below outside the core.
reconstruction: Stability is \(H_N\ge-BN\); Mayer integrability is \(\int|e^{-\beta\Phi(x)}-1|dx<\infty\). The ensemble and small parameter are supplied. This does not alone establish every canonical fixed-density limit or equivalence of ensembles.
fate: \citet[\S\S1--3]{minlos1967limiting}, received 20 December 1966, is the close construction. The canonical limiting-measure hypothesis is separately identified by \citet[Lecture II, pp.~150--152]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved in dilute regimes; unrestricted density, uniqueness and complete phase diagrams are different questions.

title: Uniform mixing and its quantifiers
notes: Separated cylinder events satisfy \(\mu(A\cap B)-\mu(A)\mu(B)\to0\), with the gloss “uniformly over all pairs \(U\)”; the limiting measure is said to have this property.
statement: The later lecture formulation fixes bounded \(U\) and \(A\in\mathcal F_U\), then asks for \(\sup_{V:\operatorname{dist}(U,V)\ge r}\sup_{B\in\mathcal F_V}|\mu(A\cap B)-\mu(A)\mu(B)|\to0\). Uniformity over unrestricted sizes of both windows is stronger. Pointwise correlation convergence does not by itself supply either uniformity or a quantitative variance bound.
reconstruction: The fixed-event quantifier is taken from the expanded lectures, not silently substituted into the diplomatic transcription. The 1967 existence paper explicitly defers the mixing/ergodicity discussion.
fate: \citet[Lecture II, formula (2.5), pp.~151--152]{minlos1968lectures} states the careful version and its general-regime hypothesis status; low-density cluster theory already appears in \citet{ruelle1964cluster}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: qualified dilute clustering is established, but the notebook's unrestricted gloss is unsupported.

title: Ergodic mean density
notes: Almost every configuration has a mean density, by Birkhoff's theorem and ergodicity.
statement: For a translation-invariant ergodic point-process law with finite intensity \(\rho=\mathbb E N_{[0,1)^\nu}\), growing cubes satisfy \(N_{Q_R}/|Q_R|\to\rho\) almost surely. Without ergodicity the limit is an invariant conditional expectation and can be random.
reconstruction: Finite intensity and a specified averaging sequence are added. The assertion is a law of large numbers, not a rate or central limit theorem.
fate: This application of the spatial ergodic theorem is restated in \citet[Lecture II, p.~152]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; mixing is stronger than necessary.

title: Characterizing correlation hierarchies
notes: Gelfand proposes starting with axioms on correlation functions and asks how to single them out.
statement: Given a full hierarchy of symmetric locally finite factorial correlation measures with \(\rho_0=1\), characterize when it is realized by a probability law on locally finite configurations. The key positivity condition tests finite configuration polynomials \(KG(\gamma)=\sum_{\eta\subset\gamma,\ |\eta|<\infty}G(\eta)\): if \(KG\ge0\) pointwise, then the corresponding integral against the correlation measure must be nonnegative. Symmetry, this positivity and normalization characterize realizability in Lenard's correlation-measure framework; uniqueness is separate.
reconstruction: This is a precise reconstruction of the one-line proposal. Entrywise nonnegativity of the correlations is insufficient. Full-hierarchy realizability differs from a truncated pair-correlation problem.
fate: \citet[abstract and main characterization]{lenard1975characterization} gives necessary and sufficient conditions and explicitly permits nonunique realizations; \citet{lenard1973correlation} treats determinacy.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established at the level of an infinite family of positivity conditions.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Partition function and thermodynamic limit
notes: The notes define \(Z=N!^{-1}\int e^{-\beta H}da\), say \(E,P,S,F\) are expressed through \(\log Z\), and promise \(\lim N^{-1}\log Z\).
statement: For stable tempered classical pair potentials, regular expanding vessels and fixed admissible density \(N/|\Omega|\to\rho>0\), the thermodynamic limit defines configurational free energy per particle through \(-(\beta N)^{-1}\log Z_{\Omega,N}\). Stability excludes collapse, decay controls long-range tails, and admissibility excludes impossible hard-core densities. Existence of this limit does not automatically imply convergence of every derivative.
reconstruction: The potential assumptions and regular vessel sequence are absent from this page. Full phase-space normalization adds a known momentum contribution. No all-shapes assertion is inferred.
fate: The expanded account is \citet[Lecture IV, \S\S1--4, pp.~164--176]{minlos1968lectures}; the thermodynamic-limit programme predates this talk.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established under stability and decay assumptions, compatible with phase-boundary nondifferentiability.

title: Mean energy and temperature differentiation
notes: \(E=\langle H\rangle=-\partial_\beta\log Z\), with \(\langle H\rangle\approx Ne(v,\beta)\) for pair interactions; representativeness is said to have been proved.
statement: For a \(\beta\)-independent Hamiltonian and fixed reference measure, finiteness of \(Z\) and of the first energy moment in a neighbourhood permits \(-\partial_\beta\log Z=\mathbb EH\). If convex functions \(f_N=N^{-1}\log Z_N\) converge on an open interval to \(f\), then \(f_N'(\beta)\to f'(\beta)\) at differentiability points of \(f\), and \(N^{-1}\mathbb EH_N\to-f'(\beta)\).
reconstruction: Numerator and denominator must use the same \(1/N!\) convention. Mean convergence is weaker than concentration; the latter requires fluctuation control.
fate: The identities and thermodynamic use are in \citet[Lecture IV, \S\S1--3]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard, with derivative limits qualified at phase transitions.

title: Limiting wall pressure
notes: \(p(x)=\tau_1(x)\), \(P=S^{-1}\int p\,d\sigma\); a hypothesis says wall pressure tends to a constant. The notes correctly warn that fixed-window convergence of \(\tau_1\) does not imply this.
statement: A definite theorem would require hard-wall or other boundary conditions, a family of growing vessels, a moving boundary observation point, normalization of pressure, and the exact uniformity sought. These are unspecified, so a unique modern proposition cannot be extracted.
reconstruction: For a classical hard wall the contact relation is \(\beta p_{\rm wall}=\rho_{\rm contact}\), with the appropriate mechanical stress. It is not a universal identity of pressure with a bulk correlation. Moving boundary points are outside the earlier fixed-window limit.
fate: The thermodynamic framework is present in \citet[Lecture IV]{minlos1968lectures}, but no publication establishing this unrestricted moving-wall assertion was verified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: insufficiently specified to label solved or open; the distinction of limiting procedures is valid.

title: Pressure normalization
notes: The manuscript writes \(p=\partial_V\log Z\).
statement: Physical pressure with \(k_B=1\) is \(p=\beta^{-1}(\partial_V\log Z)_{\beta,N}\), whenever a differentiable family of vessel deformations defines the derivative. The written equation instead holds for reduced pressure \(\beta p\).
reconstruction: The units are unspecified; the neighbouring contact-density formula suggests reduced pressure. This is a normalization ambiguity, not a certain transcription error.
fate: These conventions belong to the identities reviewed by \citet[Lecture IV]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established after fixing units and the volume variation.

title: Entropy sign and temperature factor
notes: The scan has \(S=\int\pi\log\pi\) and \(S/N=N^{-1}\log Z-\beta^{-1}\partial_\beta(N^{-1}\log Z)\).
statement: For \(\pi=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H}\), Gibbs entropy is \(S=-\int\pi\log\pi=\log Z+\beta\mathbb EH=\log Z-\beta\partial_\beta\log Z\). Thus \(S/N=f_N-\beta f_N'\). An opposite entropy sign convention changes both terms consistently.
reconstruction: Substitution of \(\log\pi=-\beta H-\log Z\) verifies the correction without a thermodynamic-limit theorem. Both discrepancies are present in the handwriting.
fate: The corrected identity is standard in \citet[Lecture IV, \S1]{minlos1968lectures}; the two notebook formulae cannot share a consistent convention.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false as written; the correction is completely determined.

title: Entropy per particle
notes: The limit of entropy per particle is asserted.
statement: If \(f_N=N^{-1}\log Z_N\) converges on an open interval to differentiable \(f\), convex convergence gives \(S_N/N\to f(\beta)-\beta f'(\beta)\). At a nondifferentiability point this argument provides no unique limit without a state or one-sided prescription.
reconstruction: This sufficient formulation covers a regular single-phase regime without inferring differentiability merely from existence of free energy.
fate: The relevant expanded account is \citet[Lecture IV, \S\S1--3]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard with the phase qualification.

title: Three compatible linear structures
notes: The Euclidean metric, multiplication by \(i\), and \([x,y]=(Ix,y)\) are introduced. The pairwise intersections of their preserving groups all equal \(U(n)\).
statement: If \(g\) is positive definite and \(J^2=-I\), \(g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)\), then \(\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)\) is nondegenerate skew symmetric. Preserving any two of \(g,J,\omega\) preserves the third. Thus the pairwise intersections of \(O(2n)\), \(GL(n,\mathbb C)\), and \(Sp(2n,\mathbb R)\) equal \(U(n)\).
reconstruction: Compatibility of \(g\) and \(J\) is explicit; arbitrary metric and complex structures need not satisfy the assertion.
fate: This linear algebra is Lemma 1.1 of \citet[\S1.1]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Isotropic and Lagrangian spaces
notes: An \(n\)-plane with vanishing symplectic form is Lagrangian. Real and imaginary planes are examples; planes are said to have dimension at most \(n\), and every curve for \(n=1\) is Lagrangian.
statement: An isotropic subspace \(W\subset V^{2n}\) satisfies \(\omega|_W=0\), hence \(\dim W\le n\). It is Lagrangian when \(\dim W=n\), equivalently \(W=W^\omega\). An immersed \(n\)-manifold is Lagrangian when all tangent spaces are. Every immersed curve in a symplectic surface satisfies this.
reconstruction: The inequality concerns isotropic spaces; “Lagrangian” means maximal dimension. A singular arbitrary curve need not be a submanifold.
fate: These are the definitions used in \citet[\S1.2]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard with the terminology clarified.

title: Generating functions for Lagrangian graphs
notes: The graph \(p=p(q)\) is Lagrangian if and only if \(p=\partial S/\partial q\).
statement: For a smooth one-form \(\alpha=\sum p_i(q)dq_i\) on \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\), its cotangent graph is Lagrangian exactly when \(d\alpha=0\). Locally this is equivalent to \(\alpha=dS\). Globally it is equivalent to exactness, and holds in particular for simply connected \(U\).
reconstruction: The local qualification is missing. A closed angular one-form on an annulus has a Lagrangian graph but no globally single-valued primitive.
fate: This is the standard generating-function example in the framework of \citet[\S1]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct locally; exactness is required globally.

title: Lagrangian Grassmannian as a homogeneous space
notes: \(U(n)\) acts transitively and \(O(n)\) stabilizes the real plane, so \(\Lambda(n)=U(n)/O(n)\).
statement: A real orthonormal basis of any Lagrangian plane extends complex linearly to a unitary map. The stabilizer of the standard real plane is exactly \(O(n)\), yielding a smooth identification \(\Lambda(n)\cong U(n)/O(n)\).
reconstruction: A compatible metric presents the homogeneous space; Lagrangian subspaces themselves are defined by the symplectic form.
fate: This is Lemma 1.2 in \citet[\S1.2]{arnold1967characteristic}, already submitted when the lecture was given.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; A records the matched authorial exposition rather than priority for elementary linear algebra.

title: Determinant-square fibration
notes: Determinant squared descends to \(\Lambda(n)\) because orthogonal determinants are \(\pm1\); a diagram relates \(SO,O,S^0\), \(SU,U,S^1\), and \(S\Lambda,\Lambda,S^1\).
statement: The map \(d([U])=(\det U)^2\) from \(U(n)/O(n)\) to \(S^1\) is well defined. Its fibre over one is \(SU(n)/SO(n)\), since a determinant-minus-one representative can be adjusted by a real reflection. Quotient maps and squaring on \(S^1\) give the commutative diagram of fibrations.
reconstruction: The reflection argument identifies the handwritten \(S\Lambda\). The vertical maps are not all inclusions.
fate: This is the construction of \citet[\S1.3]{arnold1967characteristic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the standard universal Maslov construction.

title: Maslov cohomology class
notes: The tangent map \(M\to\Lambda(n)\to S^1\) assigns a loop the degree of its final circle map, yielding a class in \(H^1(M,\mathbb Z)\).
statement: For a Lagrangian immersion \(i:M\to\mathbb R^{2n}\), use the ambient trivialization and tangent Gauss map \(\tau(x)=di_x(T_xM)\). Then \(\mu_M=(d\circ\tau)^*\eta\in H^1(M;\mathbb Z)\), for the chosen generator \(\eta\) on the circle. Evaluation on a loop is its winding number under \(d\circ\tau\).
reconstruction: The ambient trivialization is available in this phase space. A general symplectic ambient manifold requires the appropriate relative formulation. The doubtful “katsikl” means cocycle/class in this mathematical context.
fate: \citet[\S\S1--2]{arnold1967characteristic} develops the class already implicit in occurrence 1964-21.3; submission preceded the talk and publication followed it.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, with an orientation-dependent sign convention.

title: Morse index and quantization
notes: The Maslov index occurs in asymptotic formulae; the Morse index is obtained by counting conjugate points of a geodesic. Another geometric definition by Maslov is mentioned.
statement: For a nondegenerate fixed-endpoint geodesic segment, the index of the second variation equals the sum of interior conjugate-point multiplicities. The relative Maslov index of the path of Jacobi-data Lagrangian subspaces gives the same integer under consistent sign and endpoint conventions. In semiclassical quantization it measures caustic phase changes.
reconstruction: A relative path index is required; an arbitrary closed-loop winding number is not automatically a Morse index. The alternative definition is not actually recorded.
fate: These applications belong to \citet[\S\S2--3]{arnold1967characteristic}; the Morse index theorem itself is older.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with multiplicities and endpoint conventions.

title: Tensor decomposition and intertwiner data
notes: For a finite or compact \(G\), irreducible finite-dimensional spaces \(A_i\) are given, together with \(A_i\otimes A_k\cong\sum A_j\) and component maps \(d_{ik}^j\).
statement: For a compact topological group, finite-dimensional continuous unitary representations are completely reducible. Every tensor product \(V_i\otimes V_k\) decomposes as a finite direct sum of irreducibles with multiplicity spaces, and a choice of unitary decomposition gives intertwining maps. A general compact group can have infinitely many irreducible isomorphism classes, even though each individual tensor product is finite dimensional.
reconstruction: The notebook's finite list \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) is appropriate to a finite group or a selected finite list, not to all irreducibles of an arbitrary compact group. The phrase “each 1500 times” illustrates a sufficiently large ambient direct sum rather than a universal multiplicity bound.
fate: This is classical compact-group representation theory, the concrete category recalled by \citet[summary]{doplicherroberts1989duality}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; multiplicity spaces and actual intertwining maps are different levels of information.

title: Fusion multiplicities do not determine even a finite group
notes: The crossed-out and inserted line is transcribed as saying that properties of the tensor multiplicities recover a finite group, although not a compact group.
statement: If only the fusion coefficients and dimensions of irreducibles are meant, the assertion is false. The dihedral group of order eight and the quaternion group each have four one-dimensional complex irreducibles forming \(C_2\times C_2\), and one two-dimensional irreducible \(W\), with \(\chi\otimes W=W\) and \(W\otimes W=\bigoplus_\chi\chi\). They are not isomorphic: their numbers of involutions differ.
reconstruction: This elementary countercheck \ours\ is supplied here. It tests precisely the reading “multiplicities alone”; extra tensor coherence or intertwiner data could change the claim. The overwritten sentence remains a textual ambiguity.
fate: Classical Tannaka reconstruction uses more than a representation ring. The required categorical data are explicit in the comparison drawn by \citet[summary]{doplicherroberts1989duality}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false on the multiplicity-only reading. No unsolved finite-group reconstruction problem is inferred.

title: Tannaka reconstruction requires unit and reality conditions
notes: Replace all representation matrices \(T_i(g)\) by arbitrary linear maps \(C_i\) satisfying the displayed tensor intertwining equations; the notes claim every solution comes from a group element.
statement: Let \(\mathcal R(G)\) be the rigid symmetric category of finite-dimensional continuous unitary representations of compact \(G\), and \(F\) its forgetful functor to Hilbert spaces. The group of unitary tensor-natural automorphisms of \(F\), with \(C_{\mathbf1}=1\), is naturally \(G\), with its compact topology. The naturality conditions include all intertwiners and dual compatibility.
reconstruction: Unqualified equations admit the zero family unless unit normalization is imposed. Merely complex linear tensor automorphisms need not be unitary; even for \(S^1\) the character family \(C_k=z^k\), \(z\in\mathbb C^\times\), exhibits the missing compact reality condition.
fate: The classical concrete duality predates the seminar. \citet[summary and references 18, 27]{doplicherroberts1989duality} explicitly contrasts it with their later abstract symmetric \(C^*\)-category reconstruction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with unitary tensor-natural data; the literal unrestricted matrix formulation is false.

title: An unspecified extension to SL(2,R)
notes: The report ends “There is a generalization to \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\)”.
statement: No class of representations, topology, dual object, admissible tensor operations or reconstruction statement is given. Consequently the particular noncompact duality theorem intended cannot be identified from this sentence.
reconstruction: Finite-dimensional representations alone, all unitary representations, and operator-algebraic duality lead to materially different statements. A general later noncompact duality theorem cannot be treated as an exact match.
fate: The later literature cited in \citet[references 28--29]{doplicherroberts1989duality} supplies possible noncompact leads, not an identification of this report.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: unresolved identification rather than a demonstrated open problem.

title: Short-time heat kernel and intrinsic distance
notes: For \(\partial_tu=\sum a^{ij}(x)u_{x_ix_j}\) with point-source initial data, the notes give \(u=\exp[-g(x,y)/t+o(t^{-1})]\) and identify \(g=d^2\) for the metric generated by \(a^{ij}\).
statement: For a smooth symmetric uniformly positive definite coefficient matrix \(a(x)\), with standard boundedness assumptions ensuring the positive fundamental solution on \(\mathbb R^n\), put \(g_x(v,v)=v^\top a(x)^{-1}v\). Then \(\lim_{t\downarrow0}-4t\log p(t,x,y)=d_g(x,y)^2\). Equivalently \(p(t,x,y)=\exp[-d_g(x,y)^2/(4t)+o(t^{-1})]\) for fixed \(x,y\).
reconstruction: The inverse matrix defines the metric. Uniform ellipticity and a standard global coefficient setting are supplied as sufficient hypotheses. The normalization is for the displayed generator with no factor \(1/2\).
fate: \citet[pp.~431--455]{varadhan1967fundamental} is the exact subsequent paper by Varadhan, reported here by Nirenberg. Publisher metadata was checked; the normalization is independently fixed by the notebook's Gaussian.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The literal identification of \(g\) in the exponent is off by a factor four.

title: Gaussian normalization and subleading powers of time
notes: The Euclidean example is \(Ct^{-n/2}\exp[-|x-y|^2/(4t)]\); the polynomial factor is said to enter the \(o(t^{-1})\) term.
statement: For \(\partial_tu=\Delta u\), \(p(t,x,y)=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}\exp[-|x-y|^2/(4t)]\). Since \(t\log t\to0\), \(\log(t^{-n/2})=o(t^{-1})\), so this prefactor does not affect \(-4t\log p\).
reconstruction: The constant is supplied from mass-one normalization. Direct differentiation and Gaussian integration independently check the formula and its factor four.
fate: This classical example is the normalization check for the general result \citep{varadhan1967fundamental}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard and correct.

title: Composition expansion with a controlled remainder
notes: \(AB=C_0+\cdots+C_{s-1}+T_s\), with \(\sigma(C_k)=\sum_{|\alpha|=k}(\alpha!)^{-1}\partial_\xi^\alpha a\,D_x^\alpha b\); \(T_s\) has order \(\sigma+\lambda-s\).
statement: For properly supported classical or \(S^{m}_{1,0}\) operators \(A,B\) of orders \(m_1,m_2\), the Kohn--Nirenberg product symbol satisfies \(a\# b-\sum_{|\alpha|<N}(\alpha!)^{-1}\partial_\xi^\alpha a\,D_x^\alpha b\in S^{m_1+m_2-N}_{1,0}\), with \(D_x=(1/i)\partial_x\). In particular the principal symbol is \(a_{m_1}b_{m_2}\).
reconstruction: The symbol class, support/localization conditions and Fourier convention are supplied. Symbol estimates are essential; a formal Taylor polynomial alone does not bound the remainder.
fate: This is the already published calculus of \citet{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}. The notebook's formula was checked directly against P000168; external verification here is bibliographic rather than a full rereading of those papers.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard pseudodifferential composition.

title: Fourier-space proof of the composition formula
notes: The localized Fourier kernels \(\widetilde h(\xi-\eta,\eta)\), \(\widetilde g(\eta-\tau,\tau)\) are composed; Taylor expansion of the second variable of \(\widetilde h\) at \(\eta=\tau\) gives derivatives and convolution products.
statement: With compact spatial localization and the preceding symbol estimates, write the composition as an oscillatory double integral. Taylor-expand \(a(x,\xi+\eta)\) in \(\eta\); transfer each \(\eta^\alpha\) to \(D_x^\alpha b\) by Fourier inversion. The integral Taylor remainder and integration by parts yield the order \(m_1+m_2-N\) estimate.
reconstruction: The notebook gives the algebraic part of this proof but omits remainder estimates and convergence regularization. They are hypotheses and standard analytic steps required for the theorem, not additional recorded calculations.
fate: The method is part of the original symbol calculus \citep{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the recorded proof is a sketch of the composition theorem.

title: Formal asymptotic symbol
notes: For homogeneous \(A_k\) of orders \(\tau_k\searrow-\infty\), \(A\sim\sum A_k\) means the remainder after \(N\) terms has order below \(\tau_N\); the formal sum of \(a_k\) is called the symbol.
statement: In the classical calculus a full formal symbol is a sequence \(a_{m-j}(x,\xi)\), homogeneous of degree \(m-j\) for \(|\xi|\ge1\), such that \(a-\sum_{j<N}\chi(\xi)a_{m-j}\in S^{m-N}_{1,0}\) for every \(N\), with a cutoff near zero. More generally one may specify a decreasing order sequence tending to \(-\infty\) with corresponding remainder bounds.
reconstruction: This distinguishes a formal homogeneous expansion from an exact total symbol. The notebook's weaker “order below \(\tau_N\)” does not itself specify the sharper conventional next-order bound.
fate: Asymptotic symbols were part of the 1965 calculus \citep{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard after a remainder convention is fixed.

title: Zero formal symbol and smoothing operators
notes: “Symbol zero” means \(A\) has order \(-\infty\).
statement: For a properly supported classical operator, vanishing of every homogeneous formal-symbol component is equivalent to membership in \(\Psi^{-\infty}\). Such an operator has a smooth kernel and maps compactly supported distributions to smooth functions; on a closed manifold it improves every Sobolev order.
reconstruction: A zero principal symbol merely lowers order; it is the entire formal expansion that must vanish.
fate: This is the smoothing ideal of the established calculus \citep{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard and correct with the meaning of “symbol” fixed.

title: Uniqueness of the formal homogeneous expansion
notes: The theorem says an operator's symbol is uniquely determined.
statement: For a fixed coordinate system and quantization, the homogeneous components of a classical symbol are uniquely determined by the operator modulo smoothing. Two distinct homogeneous leading terms cannot differ by a lower-order symbol. An exact total symbol depends on localization and quantization, and transforms nontrivially under coordinate changes.
reconstruction: The uniqueness is of the formal expansion in a fixed calculus, not of a coordinate-invariant scalar full symbol.
fate: This is the uniqueness convention in the calculus of \citet{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard after conventions are fixed.

title: Realization of a formal symbol
notes: The notes assert that for every symbol there exists an operator.
statement: Given smooth homogeneous components \(a_{m-j}\) satisfying the symbol bounds on each compact coordinate set, an asymptotic summation using cutoffs at successively larger frequencies constructs \(a\in S^m_{1,0}\) with that formal expansion. Quantization and localization give an operator, unique modulo smoothing for the prescribed expansion.
reconstruction: “Every symbol” means an admissible formal classical symbol, not an arbitrary collection without smoothness or local estimates. The cutoff construction is a Borel-type asymptotic summation.
fate: This realization theorem is already part of the 1965 calculus \citep{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established.

title: Filtered algebra of pseudodifferential operators
notes: Pseudodifferential operators form an algebra and their formal product is \(\sum_\alpha(\alpha!)^{-1}\partial_\xi^\alpha\sigma(A)D_x^\alpha\sigma(B)\).
statement: Properly supported classical operators form a filtered algebra: \(\Psi^{m_1}\Psi^{m_2}\subset\Psi^{m_1+m_2}\), with the written asymptotic symbol product. The smoothing operators form a two-sided ideal, so this product descends to complete formal symbols modulo smoothing.
reconstruction: The conclusion is the algebraic organization of the preceding composition and realization theorems; it requires the same support and symbol-class hypotheses.
fate: This is the central already published result named in the title of \citet{kohnnirenberg1965algebra}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard calculus; no undeveloped research proposal is present.

title: Planar incompressible Navier--Stokes and Euler systems
notes:
The notes display both momentum equations for \(u,v\), the pressure gradient, \(
u\Delta u,
u\Delta v\), and \(u_x+v_y=0\); \(
u=0\) is called Euler's ideal-fluid system.
statement:
For constant density \(ho>0\) and kinematic viscosity \(
u>0\), a smooth planar velocity \(w=(u,v)\) obeys \(\partial_tw+(w\cdot
abla)w=-ho^{-1}
abla p+
u\Delta w\), \(
abla\cdot w=0\). The formal zero-viscosity equations are the incompressible Euler system. This algebraic substitution alone is not a convergence theorem.
reconstruction: The vector notation condenses the two correctly written component equations. Boundary and initial conditions are a separate part of either problem.
fate: These are the classical governing equations used in \citet[\S1]{oleinik1968boundary}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard equations; the boundary-condition issue is the next item.

title: Why vanishing viscosity is singular at a wall
notes: The incompressible planar Navier--Stokes equations are written. Setting viscosity to zero gives Euler, but the viscous terms cannot simply be discarded because no-slip and ideal-fluid boundary conditions differ.
statement: At a stationary impermeable wall, viscous no-slip imposes both velocity components zero, whereas impermeable Euler flow imposes only the normal component zero. If the limiting outer tangential velocity is nonzero, convergence to that Euler field cannot be uniform up to the wall. A thin transition region is therefore required in the classical matched-asymptotic picture.
reconstruction: This observation does not prove a Navier--Stokes-to-Prandtl limit, a boundary-layer thickness theorem, or formation of a layer for all initial data.
fate: This is the classical Prandtl motivation reviewed by \citet[\S1]{oleinik1968boundary}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the boundary-condition mismatch is established; a rigorous inviscid limit requires additional hypotheses.

title: The Prandtl system and outer pressure
notes: The tangential equation retains \(\nu u_{yy}\), continuity remains, and the pressure is a prescribed function \(p(t,x)\) constant in the normal direction. Although \(p_y=0\) is crossed out in the display, the prose explicitly retains its meaning.
statement: In boundary-layer coordinates at a flat wall, the Prandtl model is \(u_t+uu_x+vu_y=\nu u_{yy}-\rho^{-1}p_x(t,x)\), \(u_x+v_y=0\). Matching to the outer tangential Euler velocity \(U(t,x)\) imposes \(U_t+UU_x=-\rho^{-1}p_x\). The formal scaling \(y=\sqrt{\nu}\,Y\), with the normal velocity scaled accordingly, explains the retained normal diffusion.
reconstruction: The outer Bernoulli equation and the distinction between physical and rescaled variables are supplied. The formal derivation is not a proved approximation theorem.
fate: The displayed model is the one studied in \citet[p.~751, equations (1)--(3)]{oleinik1966system} and \citet[\S1]{oleinik1968boundary}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard boundary-layer equations.

title: Correctly posed initial and inflow data
notes: The wall conditions are \(u=0\), \(v=v_0(x,t)\); the notebook writes inconsistent arguments in \(u|_{x=0}=u_0(x)\) and \(u|_{t=0}=u_0(x,t)\), and requires \(u\to U(t,x)\) as \(y\to\infty\).
statement: On \(0<x<X\), \(y>0\), \(t>0\), prescribe \(u(t,x,0)=0\), \(v(t,x,0)=v_0(t,x)\), initial profile \(u(0,x,y)=u_0(x,y)\), inflow profile \(u(t,0,y)=u_1(t,y)\), and \(\lim_{y\to\infty}u(t,x,y)=U(t,x)\). These data must agree at their intersections, satisfy the wall compatibility equations, and match \(U\) at infinity.
reconstruction: Distinct \(u_0,u_1\) and their variables are reconstructed from the PDE and checked in Oleinik's paper. The notebook's variable mistakes are faithful errors, not proof of a different problem.
fate: The correctly indexed data are explicit in \citet[p.~751]{oleinik1966system}; the note was received 1 March 1966 and published before this October report.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the standard initial/inflow Prandtl problem under a specified solution class.

title: Local existence and uniqueness in the monotone class
notes: The solution is said to be unique if it exists, and to exist on \(0\le t\le T\) over the whole body; separation may occur later but not instantaneously.
statement: A sufficient classical setting is \(U>c>0\), smooth compatible data with \(u_0,u_1>0\) for \(y>0\), \(\partial_yu_0,\partial_yu_1>0\), convergence to \(U\) at infinity, and two-sided tail bounds \(c_1(U-u_j)\le\partial_yu_j\le c_2(U-u_j)\), together with the bounded weighted derivatives and corner compatibility in Oleinik's Theorem 4. There is then a unique classical monotone solution for sufficiently short time on a finite streamwise interval.
reconstruction: The notebook omits this crucial monotone solution class. The complete derivative and compatibility package is specified by the cited theorem rather than an assertion about all smooth data. The Crocco transformation uses monotonicity to replace the normal coordinate by the velocity.
fate: \citet[pp.~751--754]{oleinik1966system} already announced this theory; \citet[Theorem 4, pp.~28--29]{oleinik1968boundary} supplies its detailed sufficient assumptions.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the monotone class; no arbitrary-data well-posedness statement is valid.

title: All-time existence on a short inflow interval
notes: Near the beginning of the flow around the body, the solution exists for all time. The inequality \(p_x\le0\) appears separately beneath this statement.
statement: Under the uniform-in-time data bounds and compatibility assumptions of Oleinik's Theorem 5, one can choose a sufficiently small streamwise length \(X_1>0\) so that a monotone classical solution exists for all \(t\ge0\), \(0\le x\le X_1\). This differs from global existence on the entire body. A favourable pressure gradient is an additional recorded regime, not a license to omit all other assumptions.
reconstruction: The relation of the isolated inequality to the previous sentence is not grammatically explicit. The detailed cited short-inflow theorem is the verified comparison; no universal all-time theorem for every vessel is claimed.
fate: The result announced in the 1966 theory is proved in \citet[Theorem 5, pp.~29--32]{oleinik1968boundary}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the stated short-inflow and uniform-data restrictions.

title: The scope of stability of a boundary layer
notes: The final sentence says a solution is always stable if it exists and is a “nast.” boundary layer; the abbreviation is not safely expanded.
statement: Oleinik-type monotone solutions have stability/continuous-dependence statements in the corresponding controlled class and norms. Existence of a smooth Prandtl solution alone does not imply Sobolev stability: linearization around suitable nonmonotone shear profiles with a nondegenerate critical point has high-frequency instability.

fate: The monotone framework is in \citet{oleinik1968boundary}; the nonmonotone obstruction is the result of \citet[Theorem 1, author version pp.~4--5]{gerardvaretdormy2010illposed}, first circulated in 2009 and published in 2010.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal sentence is underdetermined; general Sobolev stability is false, while qualified monotone theory is established.

title: Helgason's support problem for geodesic spheres
notes: On a complete negatively curved manifold, \(f\in C^\infty_0\); if every sphere enclosing a given ball \(B\) has zero surface integral of \(f\), prove \(f=0\) outside \(B\). The name Helgason is written twice.
statement: Let \(M\) be a complete simply connected smooth Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature, \(B\) a closed geodesic ball, and \(f\in C_c^\infty(M)\). If \(\int_{S(y,r)}f\,d\sigma=0\) for every geodesic sphere whose closed ball \(D(y,r)\) contains \(B\), must \(\operatorname{supp}f\subset B\)?
reconstruction: Simple connectivity is supplied from the exact published formulation, making geodesic spheres globally regular by the Hadamard setting. “Sphere containing \(B\)” means its enclosed ball contains \(B\), not that the hypersurface contains the ball as a subset. The transform is spherical integration, not the geodesic ray transform.
fate: This is exactly \citet[Problem 4.1]{quinto2008helgason}. That work proves the real-analytic metric case through its support theorems, including Theorem 5.1; it does not remove analyticity for an arbitrary smooth negatively curved metric.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the real-analytic case is verified; no resolution of the full smooth-metric statement was located in the targeted searches. The classification concerns this precise remaining regularity gap, not generic integral geometry.
worth: Worth revisiting through smooth local support estimates, but the available evidence does not justify a bounded new theorem in this run.

title: Entire convex solutions of the constant Monge--Ampere equation
notes: Calabi's problem asks whether a convex function on \(\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\det D^2u=1\) must be a polynomial of degree two; the notes mention \(n=2\) and Calabi's \(n\le5\) result.
statement: Every convex entire \(C^2\) solution of \(\det D^2u=1\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) is \(u(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax+b\cdot x+c\), where \(A\) is positive definite and \(\det A=1\). The modern theorem extends to convex viscosity solutions.
reconstruction: “Entire” and convexity are essential. The conclusion permits affine terms and arbitrary positive definite Hessian of determinant one; it does not say the Hessian is the identity.
fate: The all-dimensional result is the J\"orgens--Calabi--Pogorelov theorem. \citet[Introduction and Theorem 1.1, pp.~549--550]{caffarellili2003extension} gives the exact modern statement and records the sequence from J\"orgens's \(n=2\) result through Calabi to Pogorelov's all-dimensional resolution. The all-dimensional paper \citep{pogorelov1972improper} was received in June 1971 and published in 1972; its metadata, rather than its full proof, was checked.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: settled affirmatively in every dimension.

title: The dimension-dependent Bernstein problem

For \(u\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{div}(

title: Recovering the metric from a Sobolev pullback isometry
notes: The notes give the \(H^1\) inner product \(\int\varphi\psi+\int\langle d\varphi,d\psi\rangle\) and the Dirichlet energy. An \(H^1\) isometry inducing a diffeomorphism between \(M\) and \(M'\) should imply a Riemannian isometry.
statement: Let \(F:M\to M'\) be a smooth diffeomorphism of closed smooth Riemannian manifolds. If the pullback \(u\mapsto u\circ F\) preserves the full \(H^1\) inner product for every smooth \(u,v\), then \(F^*g'=g\). An arbitrary abstract Hilbert-space isometry does not suffice.
reconstruction: “Inducing a diffeomorphism” is interpreted as composition pullback. Elementary verification \ours: testing the inner product against \(1\) shows \(F\) preserves volume. Subtracting the resulting \(L^2\) identity leaves equality of Dirichlet forms. In local coordinates their difference is \(\int q^{ij}\partial_i u\,\partial_jv=0\) for all compactly supported \(u,v\). Integration by parts gives \(\partial_j(q^{ij}\partial_i u)=0\); choose \(du=0\) and an arbitrary Hessian at a point to obtain \(q^{ij}=0\), hence equality of inverse metrics. A second check via equality of the principal symbols of the associated Laplacians gives the same conclusion.
fate: This precise pullback version follows by the displayed elementary argument. The later stronger reconstruction from an order isomorphism intertwining heat semigroups is \citet[Theorem 1.1]{arendt2017diffusion}, first circulated in 2011 and published in 2017; it is a partial, not exact historical match.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: settled under the composition interpretation. No solution of an unspecified abstract Hilbert-space reconstruction problem is claimed.
speaker: Unattributed differential-geometry discussion

title: Laplace eigenvalues are invariants, not complete metric data
notes: The line following the Sobolev question says “Invariants: eigenvalues of the Laplace operator”.
statement: A Riemannian isometry intertwines the Laplace--Beltrami operators and preserves their spectra with multiplicities. Conversely, equality of spectra alone does not imply isometry: an abstract unitary spectral identification need not preserve multiplication, order or the composition action of a map.

fate: \citet[Introduction]{arendt2017diffusion} recalls Milnor's 1964 isospectral nonisometric examples and explains the additional order structure used in reconstruction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: spectral invariance is established; isospectral nonisometric manifolds are known.

title: Evaluation map from the first Laplace eigenspace
notes: For compact irreducible symmetric \(M\), \(V\) is the eigenspace of the smallest nonzero Laplace eigenvalue and \(\varphi:M\to V^*\) is written.

Evaluation defines \(\varphi(x)(f)=f(x)\) in \(V^*\), after choosing the \(L^2\) inner product if one wants \(V^*\cong V\). The map is equivariant under isometries. If \(M\) is an irreducible compact symmetric space, its induced symmetric quadratic tensor is an invariant multiple of the metric.

title: Smooth type of a manifold with equally long closed geodesics
notes: The next numbered problem asks whether compact simply connected \(M\), all of whose geodesics are closed and have the same length, is diffeomorphic to a symmetric space “of the first type”. A rank-like expression is crossed out.
statement: The standard intended topology question is: if every unit-speed prime geodesic of a closed simply connected Riemannian manifold has the same period, must the manifold be diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space, namely a sphere, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley plane?
reconstruction: Rank one is a contextual identification, not a perfectly legible manuscript word. “Same length” means prime periods, since arbitrary iterates have different lengths. This topology problem is distinct from the Blaschke metric-rigidity conjecture and from the Berger conjecture about equality of periods.
fate: The cohomological restrictions below are established. \citet[definition on p.~1 and Main Theorem on p.~3]{lisong2026zoll} use the stronger Zoll hypothesis that every unit-speed prime geodesic is simple closed and all have the same period. Under that hypothesis and the additional entire-Grauert-tube assumption, they prove metric rigidity of the complex-projective cohomology type, up to scale. Simplicity is not explicit in the notebook, nor is an entire Grauert tube assumed; the result supplies no general diffeomorphism classification under its recorded hypotheses.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: no full smooth classification was verified; the remaining issue is the diffeomorphism type beyond the known cohomology restrictions. The recent additional-hypothesis theorem is not counted as a solution of that issue.
worth: Worth pursuing through precise topological obstructions or restricted geometric classes, but no new bounded contribution is established here.

title: Nonround metrics with all geodesics closed
notes: There is an analytic manifold diffeomorphic to a sphere but not isometric to it, in the preceding closed-geodesic context.
statement: There exist nonround real-analytic metrics on \(S^2\) for which every prime geodesic is simple closed and has the same length. Consequently the conclusion sought in the preceding problem cannot be equality with the round metric merely from the closed-geodesic hypothesis.
reconstruction: “Not isometric” is interpreted relative to a standard round sphere after scale normalization. The source does not supply the metric, and no formula for a new example is invented.
fate: The historical nonround Zoll examples, beginning in 1903, are recalled by \citet[Introduction, p.~2]{lisong2026zoll}; they predate the seminar.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established and compatible with the proposed diffeomorphism conclusion.

title: Bott--Samelson cohomology restriction
notes: The notes attribute to Bott the result that the preceding manifold has the same cohomological structure as the symmetric model.
statement: For a closed simply connected manifold in the all-geodesics-closed setting, Bott--Samelson theory constrains its integral cohomology ring to that of a compact rank-one symmetric space. In particular it is a truncated polynomial ring of the corresponding sphere or projective-space type; this does not determine the smooth structure.
reconstruction: The coefficient ring and distinction from diffeomorphism classification are made explicit. The attribution is broadened to the standard Bott--Samelson formulation rather than attributing every refinement to one manuscript parenthesis.
fate: The modern formulation and reference to its classical proof are given by \citet[Introduction, pp.~1--2]{lisong2026zoll}; it is an already known partial answer, not the full smooth classification.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established topological restriction.

title: Contact structures on compact three-manifolds
notes: The last question is whether every compact \(M^3\) has a contact structure.
statement: Every closed orientable smooth three-manifold admits a contact structure. The statement with no orientability assumption is false: a contact plane field locally given by \(\ker\alpha\) orients a three-manifold by \(\alpha\wedge d\alpha\), since replacement by \(f\alpha\) multiplies this volume form by \(f^2>0\). Thus a closed nonorientable example such as \(\mathbb{RP}^2\times S^1\) admits none, even if coorientation is not required.
reconstruction: The orientability correction is necessary for the literal question, not an optional modern strengthening. Compact is read as closed; boundaries require an additional convention. The local-form orientation check was independently verified by expanding \(f\alpha\wedge d(f\alpha)\). The local identity \(\alpha'=f\alpha\Rightarrow\alpha'\wedge d\alpha'=f^2\alpha\wedge d\alpha\) is checked here \ours.
fate: Martinet's affirmative orientable theorem appeared in 1971 \citep{martinet1971contact}; \citet[pp.~165--166]{eliashberg1992contact} explicitly states both the existence theorem and the orientation consequence.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: settled: yes for closed orientable three-manifolds, no for nonorientable ones.
